paragraphs.paragraph: Praise for the Lord’s Kindness, Power, and Wisdom
paragraphs.title: Praise for the Lord’s Kindness, Power, and Wisdom

answers: Because it is good and pleasant
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says that singing praises to God is good, pleasant, and comely.
easy.q: Why does the psalm call people to praise the LORD?

easy.explanation: The LORD builds Jerusalem and gathers the outcasts of Israel.
easy.q: Whom does the LORD gather together?

easy.explanation: Verse 3 says that He heals the broken in heart.

medium.explanation: The two actions together portray the restoration of the city and its scattered people.
medium.q: What connection is made between building Jerusalem and gathering Israel’s outcasts?

medium.explanation: To bind up wounds is to dress, care for, and heal them.
medium.q: What does “bindeth up their wounds” mean?

answers: The LORD knows and rules the stars
The stars are on the earth
medium.explanation: Calling every star by name emphasizes His knowledge and authority.
medium.q: What does the LORD’s naming every star show?

answers: Naming the stars and healing the brokenhearted
challenge.explanation: The passage joins His cosmic power with His compassion toward hurting people.
challenge.q: Which combination shows both the LORD’s greatness and His care for people?

challenge.explanation: The LORD lifts up the meek but casts the wicked down.

answers: He does not know the stars
challenge.explanation: Infinite understanding is understanding without limit.
challenge.q: What can be understood from “his understanding is infinite”?

paragraphs.idea: Praise for the Lord’s Kindness, Power, and Wisdom

paragraphs.paragraph: Praise for Providence, Sustenance, and Blessing Beyond Physical Strength
paragraphs.title: Praise for Providence, Sustenance, and Blessing Beyond Physical Strength

easy.explanation: Verse 7 calls the people to sing with thanksgiving and praise.
easy.q: What does the psalm call the people to do?

easy.explanation: The LORD uses the clouds to prepare rain for the earth.
easy.q: What do the clouds prepare for the earth?

answers: The beast and the young ravens
easy.explanation: Verse 9 mentions food for the beast and the young ravens.
easy.q: To whom does the LORD give food?

answers: Horses, wicked people, Jerusalem, and ice
medium.explanation: Clouds bring rain, rain supports grass, and the LORD provides food for living creatures.
medium.q: What order of providence is described in these verses?

answers: Wait and trust in His mercy
medium.explanation: To hope in His mercy is to wait for and trust in His loving kindness.
medium.q: What does “hope in his mercy” mean?

answers: They are examples of creatures the LORD feeds
medium.explanation: The young ravens illustrate the LORD’s provision for His creatures.
medium.q: Why are the young ravens mentioned?

answers: The LORD’s pleasure does not depend on physical strength
challenge.explanation: The LORD does not delight in the strength of the horse or the legs of a man.
challenge.q: What is the main idea in the contrast between the strength of a horse and fearing the LORD?

answers: Care for nature and creatures leads to the LORD’s desire for faithful people
The passage moves from Jerusalem to the stars
The passage moves from law to snow
challenge.explanation: The passage first describes provision in creation and then explains what pleases the LORD in people.
challenge.q: What connection exists between verses 8–9 and verses 10–11?

answers: His providence reaches many creatures, not only the strong
challenge.explanation: The example shows that the LORD cares for even dependent and seemingly insignificant creatures.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the LORD’s care for young ravens?

paragraphs.idea: Praise for Providence, Sustenance, and Blessing Beyond Physical Strength

easy.explanation: Verse 12 directly addresses Jerusalem and Zion.
easy.q: Who is called to praise the LORD?

easy.explanation: The LORD strengthened the bars of the city’s gates.
Verse 14 says that He fills Jerusalem with the finest of the wheat.
easy.q: With what does the LORD fill Jerusalem?

medium.explanation: The verses mention strong gates, blessed children, peace, and abundant food.
medium.q: What blessings are included in these verses?

medium.explanation: Bars are strong beams used to secure and close gates.
medium.q: What are the “bars” of the gates?

answers: Both describe the number of stars
medium.explanation: Strong gates and peaceful borders both represent safety and protection.
medium.q: How are strengthened gates and peace in the borders related?

answers: Protection, family blessing, peace, and plenty
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from secure gates and blessed children to peace and abundant food.
challenge.q: What is the main sequence of blessings given to Jerusalem?

answers: The city is presented as one that can be addressed
The city is a particular human being
challenge.explanation: The direct address gives Jerusalem and Zion a vivid, personified role.
challenge.q: What can be understood from directly addressing Jerusalem and Zion?

answers: It represents the provision of life’s needs
It describes the strength of the gates
It explains the movement of the stars
challenge.explanation: Wheat is food, so an abundant supply represents prosperity and provision.
challenge.q: Why does the finest wheat fit the description of blessing?

paragraphs.paragraph: The Lord’s Word Governing the Weather
paragraphs.title: The Lord’s Word Governing the Weather

easy.explanation: Verse 15 says that He sends His commandment upon the earth.
easy.q: Where does the LORD send His commandment?

easy.explanation: The passage names snow, hoarfrost, and ice.
His word melts the ice, and the waters flow.
easy.q: What happens after the LORD sends His word and causes His wind to blow?

answers: The speed with which His word is carried out
medium.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the LORD’s command is executed quickly.
medium.q: What does “his word runneth very swiftly” show?

medium.explanation: To scatter means to spread or throw in different directions.
medium.q: What does “scattereth” mean in “he scattereth the hoarfrost like ashes”?

answers: Cold and freezing change to melting and flowing water
Silence changes to the sound of war
Hunger changes to an abundance of wheat
medium.explanation: Snow, frost, and ice are followed by melting and flowing waters.
medium.q: What change is described between verses 16–18?

answers: The weather is subject to the LORD’s word
Snow is stronger than the LORD’s word
challenge.explanation: The same divine word brings cold and then brings about melting and flowing water.
challenge.q: What does the sequence of snow, frost, ice, wind, and water teach?

answers: The great severity of the cold
That no one may enter the city
That the stars stand in heaven
challenge.explanation: The question stresses how powerful and difficult the cold is.
challenge.q: What does the question “who can stand before his cold?” emphasize?

answers: The LORD sends His word, which acts in nature
challenge.explanation: Both verses show the LORD sending His word to accomplish His purpose.
challenge.q: What repeated verbal connection appears in verses 15 and 18?

paragraphs.idea: The Lord’s Word Governing the Weather

paragraphs.paragraph: The Torah as a Special Gift to Israel
paragraphs.title: The Torah as a Special Gift to Israel

easy.explanation: Verse 19 says that the LORD shows His word to Jacob and Israel.
easy.q: To whom does the LORD show His word?

easy.explanation: The verse specifically mentions His statutes and judgments.
easy.q: What does the LORD give Israel?

answers: With a command to build gates
easy.explanation: The final words are “Praise ye the LORD.”

answers: Israel received the LORD’s word, statutes, and judgments
Other nations received all the names of the stars
Israel received no word from the LORD
medium.explanation: The passage says that the LORD has not dealt in this way with every nation.
medium.q: What is emphasized by the comparison between Israel and other nations?

medium.explanation: In this context, “sheweth” means makes known or reveals.
medium.q: What does “sheweth” mean in “He sheweth his word unto Jacob”?

answers: To give thanks for the special gift given to Israel
medium.explanation: The passage ends in praise because Israel received the LORD’s special instruction.
medium.q: Why does praise follow the description of the statutes and judgments?

answers: The LORD rules the world and reveals His statutes to Israel
The law describes only the weather
The LORD’s greatness removes the need for praise
challenge.explanation: The psalm joins the LORD’s power over creation with His revelation to His people.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the LORD’s greatness in creation and His giving of the law?

answers: The gift described is presented as unique to Israel
Israel has no statutes or judgments
Every nation received exactly the same gift
challenge.explanation: The statement emphasizes the special privilege given to Israel.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from “He hath not dealt so with any nation”?

challenge.explanation: Verse 19 explicitly names the LORD’s statutes and judgments.
challenge.q: Which pair names two aspects of the LORD’s instruction?

paragraphs.idea: The Torah as a Special Gift to Israel
